title: Residency — active without subject enrollment (reference)
story: Nicolas Valdez is a Master of Arts in Education student in the writing stage who is not enrolled in any subject this semester. Residency keeps such a student active while he completes allowed academic work. It is separate from AWOL, Leave of Absence, withdrawal and completed standing.

Graduate School Staff open Record residency on the AWOL & Residency board, pick the student, choose a handbook purpose and the semester, run the residency policy checker and, when the evidence supports it, record the residency. Nicolas's demo record has 14 course-audit subjects still missing, so the checker asks for human review; the walkthrough shows that result as it appears.
accounts: Residency checker and record on AWOL & Residency
data: Thesis / dissertation work (other choices: Practicum / internship completion, Comprehensive examination, Awaiting research publication)
Thesis writing continues without subject enrollment; adviser confirmed progress this semester.

parts.title: Part A - Check and record the Residency
parts.intro: Nicolas's demo record is reset first (sign-in page demo reset).

steps.text: Sign in as GS Staff and open **AWOL & Residency** under Standalone Processes. The board header has a **Record residency** button; the Residency columns (Residency, Residency closed) sit at the right of the board.

shots.caption: AWOL & Residency board with the Record residency button.

steps.text: Click **Record residency**. A window opens with **Student** search, **Residency purpose**, **Semester** and **Staff verification notes**. Search "Valdez", select **Nicolas Valdez**, choose the purpose Thesis / dissertation work and the semester AY 2026-2027 1st Semester, and type the staff verification note.

shots.caption: Record residency window with Nicolas selected.

steps.text: Click **Run residency policy checker**. The residency policy review appears with the result **Needs Human Review** (advice for staff; the Dean decides). Read the checks it lists, including the handbook condition that a student with course units left who will not enroll should use LOA instead.

shots.caption: Residency policy review inside the window.

steps.text: Click **Record residency** in the window. The page confirms "Saved. The student record, queue, and monitoring indicators were updated."

parts.title: Part B - Where the record shows

steps.text: Search Nicolas on the board. His card is in the **Residency** column. Click **View details**: the window shows the tracker (Residency recorded, Residency closed), the student, type Residency, semester, purpose, the policy result (Needs Human Review), the date recorded, the staff note and the policy check (suggested for the Dean: Review or Use LOA).
Open **Students** and search Valdez. The directory row shows Nicolas with enrollment **Residency** and standing **Active**.

shots.caption: Students directory after the Residency was recorded.

notes: Residency is an active no-subject enrollment state for approved academic work. A student with remaining course units who will stop studying should use Leave of Absence instead; the checker says so in its third check.

The checker flags Nicolas as Needs Human Review because his course audit still has missing subjects. Staff can still record the residency after verifying the evidence; the case then carries the classification Needs Human Review. The Dean's decision is Not applicable for Residency.
The Residency case window can also be closed when the period ends; that was not done in this walkthrough.
